items.title: Rise in number of illustrators losing work to GenAI, survey finds
items.excerpt: An Association of Illustrators survey finds a growing number of illustrators losing work and income to generative AI, with the technology changing how much work they get and how commissions are briefed.

items.title: Publishers urge US court to reject OpenAI's fair use defence in copyright case
items.excerpt: Four publishing and copyright organisations, including the AAP and IBPA, filed an amicus brief urging a US court to reject OpenAI's fair-use defence, arguing AI training on copyrighted books threatens authors' livelihoods.

items.title: Hundreds of authors bring individual copyright claims against Meta
items.excerpt: Around 300 authors have filed individual copyright claims against Meta, alleging it copied their books to train its AI models without permission.

items.title: IFRRO Releases New Study on AI, Copyright Issues
items.excerpt: IFRRO's new report combines legal and market analysis of AI and copyright with a global survey of nearly 2,000 rightsholders and users.

items.title: Survey Finds Book Buyers Split on AI Use
items.excerpt: A BookInsights.ai study finds younger readers more open to authors using AI in some form, but readers of all ages agree books should disclose AI use.

items.title: PLA Partners with Microsoft on Library AI Info Sessions
items.excerpt: The Public Library Association and Microsoft are launching AI-literacy info sessions in public libraries starting in December, aimed at helping patrons exercise agency over AI.

items.title: Audible Lets Listeners Talk to Dracula
items.excerpt: ALLi's news podcast covers Audible's new AI feature that lets listeners converse with Dracula, plus an OpenAI copyright-case twist and the Books by People human-authorship label.

items.title: Can AI Run Your Book Marketing?
items.excerpt: Michael La Ronn and Sacha Black weigh how far indie authors can hand book marketing to AI tools in this ALLi member Q&A.

items.title: Audiobook Listeners Buy in Multiple Formats; AI Splits the Ghostwriting Market
items.excerpt: Dan Holloway on Audible's multi-format sales study, Smashwords pre-orders, and how AI is splitting the ghostwriting market.

items.title: Less Than Two Weeks After Launch, Society of Authors Withdraws from Global Ethical AI Charter
items.excerpt: The UK Society of Authors pulled out of the Ethical AI Charter it helped launch, after member backlash over its position on generative AI.

items.title: Publishers outraged at book sales to Anthropic
items.excerpt: Criticism is mounting in Japan's publishing industry after a subsidiary of distributor Nippan Group sold Japanese books to Anthropic for AI training without notifying publishers.

items.title: AI Data Companies Buying Books — US Firm Recruits in South Korea for Mass Purchases
items.excerpt: US AI data engineering firms are recruiting in South Korea to procure and scan large quantities of academic books for AI training.

items.title: Anthropic illegally trained Claude with Stanford professors' books
items.excerpt: Stanford professors whose books were pirated to train Claude opted out of the $1.5 billion settlement and filed their own lawsuit against Anthropic.

items.title: Korea Holds 1st AI Creative Contest for Children to Make Webtoons
items.excerpt: South Korea is holding its first creative contest in which children use AI tools to make webtoons.

items.title: 브레인벤쳐스, 어도비 익스체인지에 웹툰 현지화 플러그인 'ToonFlow' 공식 등록
items.excerpt: AI webtoon-localization firm Brain Ventures listed ToonFlow, a Photoshop plugin that automates speech-bubble detection, OCR, translation and lettering, on Adobe Exchange.

items.title: “사람이 쓴 소설만 읽고 싶어”…웹소설계 번지는 'AI 염증'
items.excerpt: As generative AI mass-produces web-novel manuscripts, Korean web-fiction readers are showing 'AI fatigue' and demanding human-written stories.

items.title: 에이아이투모바일 '노벨나라', AI 이중 검증 기술 적용…웹소설 품질 관리 체계 구축
items.excerpt: Web-novel platform Novelnara introduced a 'dual verification gate' combining quantitative criteria with AI evaluation, plus AI-generated background music per title.

items.title: K문학 세계화, AI로 뚫릴까…풀리지 않는 '감성 번역' 숙제
items.excerpt: As Korean literature expands abroad, AI translation is eyed to ease translator shortages and costs, but literary nuance remains an unsolved problem.

items.title: [단독] AI와 전쟁 중인 美작가조합 “한국 작가들과 협력 원한다”
items.excerpt: The US Authors Guild, fighting AI companies in court, says it wants to cooperate with Korean authors on AI and copyright.

items.title: Asian Publishers Gather in Seoul to Debate AI's Impact on Books
items.excerpt: Publishers from seven overseas markets join Korean counterparts in Seoul Nov. 3-6 for Asia Publishing Week to debate AI's impact on books and copyright.

items.title: AI 시대, 웹툰은 어떻게 살아남나…웹툰작가들이 찾은 해법
items.excerpt: The Korea Cartoonists Association's 6th Webtoon Forum discussed how webtoon creators can survive and respond to generative AI.

items.title: '하얀거탑' 작가가 묻는다…AI는 무엇을 쓰고, 못 쓰는가
items.excerpt: As generative AI spreads into webtoons, web novels and drama, a forum featuring 'White Tower' writer asks what AI can write and what only human creators can.

items.title: “AI의 약점은 실수 안 하는 것”…中 소설가 위화의 경고
items.excerpt: Chinese novelist Yu Hua says he is not worried about AI replacing writers, arguing AI's weakness is that it does not make mistakes.

items.title: Canadians open to AI narration in audiobooks, study finds
items.excerpt: NielsenIQ research finds 50% of audiobook listeners globally are now open to AI-narrated content, with Canadians also exploring more genres and formats.

items.title: France: Novel suspected of using AI removed from Renaudot Prize shortlist
items.excerpt: Thélyson Orélien's novel was excluded from the final Renaudot Prize shortlist announced Oct. 28 amid controversy over AI use in its creation.

items.title: 'Dear ChatGPT': 12-year-old wins top youth prize at Australian Poetry Slam
items.excerpt: A 12-year-old won the youth prize at the Australian Poetry Slam with 'Dear ChatGPT', a poem rejecting reliance on AI.
